name: Grilled stream fish
summary: Charcoal-grilled stream fish, also called cá suối nướng, with a rich, pungent aroma.
origin: Ban Ang. A 2012 feature of the Vietnam National Authority of Tourism names pa pỉnh tộp (cá nướng) among the local dishes. A later feature on the same site glosses it as cá suối nướng.
howToEat: Eat it as a shared plate at a Ban Ang meal. The 2012 feature does not name the herbs or the species.
The winter handbook names mắc khén and hạt dổi as seasonings Thai cooks use across this set of dishes, including cá nướng. It does not give a fish-by-fish recipe.
The hour and the price are Check on arrival.
where: Bản Áng, about 2 km south of the farm town on National Highway 43. Bao Son La’s 17 February 2023 article also names cá nướng at bản Vặt, xã Mường Sang. No restaurant is a pick.
seoTitle: Pa pinh top in Moc Chau — grilled stream fish
seoDescription: Charcoal-grilled stream fish, also called cá suối nướng, with a rich, pungent aroma.
taste: The later national-authority feature calls the aroma thơm nồng. A marinade was not printed on that line.
culture: Bao Son La’s 12 October 2016 feature writes cá suối in its Moc Chau specialty list and does not use the Thai name. The national authority uses both pa pỉnh tộp and cá suối nướng. One fish.
